standard.title: Sharing Questions, Predictions and Observations
standard.description: share questions, predictions, observations and ideas with others
standard.prior_knowledge: No formal prior science learning assumed.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students share their science questions, predictions, observations and ideas with others using a range of forms — spoken, drawn, modelled, performed or displayed.

nodes.label: Science ideas are shared with others in varied forms
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can share at least one science observation or idea with others using a chosen form (spoken, drawn, modelled, role-played or displayed).
nodes.minimum_width: Students share one science observation or idea with others using at least one form.
nodes.typical_width: Students share questions, predictions and observations through discussions and circle groups; recount experiences observing nature; show or describe how objects move; role-play how scientists use equipment; represent plant and animal features using materials; and communicate using posters, collages, digital displays, drawings or storyboards.
wider: Acknowledge and explore First Nations Australians' ways of communicating information about anatomical features of plants and animals
Role-play or show how people use different equipment to make scientific observations
Represent external features of plants and animals using blocks, modelling clay, craft materials or paper

response_modes.reason: Foundation students sharing science ideas benefit from multiple communication forms — spoken, drawn, modelled, role-played, displayed. First Nations communication forms provide a culturally rich direction that expands what counts as valid scientific communication at this level.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: First Nations communication forms provide a culturally rich direction for how science knowledge can be represented and shared in diverse ways.
success_criteria: Shares at least one science observation or idea with others
Uses at least one form beyond verbal — drawn, modelled, role-played or displayed
